card.name: Festejo
card.profile: Afro-Peruvian festive music-and-dance developed by enslaved West Africans; no musical example predates 1800 and the modern form is a mid-20th-c. reconstruction — original choreography largely lost by ~1900, standardized from 1949 with revival by José Durand, Porfirio Vásquez and Nicomedes & Victoria Santa Cruz. Dual music+dance.

observation.setting: indoor hall with painted light blue brick walls and concrete floor, with people sitting around watching an informal dance workshop or class
observation.dancers: group of mixed adults and teens, mostly women, with a female instructor leading
observation.formation_and_space: group arranged in parallel rows facing the front, following the instructor
observation.posture: torso upright or bending forward from the hips with knees slightly bent in a low athletic stance
observation.footwork: stepping side to side, taps, knee lifts, and kicks on the beat; detailed weight shifts are not clearly visible due to video resolution
observation.arms_and_hands: arms held out with curved elbows, hands gesturing, or hands placed on hips/behind back
observation.hips_and_torso: torso bends forward and arches back, subtle hip movement with knee bounces
observation.levels_jumps_turns: low level with bent knees; upper body bends down toward the floor; high kicks and leg extensions
observation.costume_and_props: casual everyday clothes, t-shirts, jeans, skirts, bare feet or casual shoes
observation.cannot_infer: exact foot placement, precise weight distribution, and subtle footwork cannot be clearly seen due to camera angle and low resolution
